title: Projective Ext computed from an injective resolution
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $M$ an $R$-module, $E$ an injective resolution of $M$, and $q\in\mathbf N$. For a module $X$, let $\operatorname{Hom}(X,E)$ be the nonnegative cochain complex of $R$-linear maps, with differential given by postcomposition. There is a natural $R$-linear isomorphism, contravariant in $X$, between Mathlib's projectively defined $\operatorname{Ext}^q_R(X,M)$ and $H^q(\operatorname{Hom}(X,E))$.

proof.text: Construct Tot Hom(P,E) and both canonical augmentations as actual cochain maps. The cited projective-edge and injective-edge theorems prove these maps are quasi-isomorphisms, by exact Hom columns and the existing first-quadrant augmentation criterion. The projective module also proves precomposition compatibility of both edges.

For each X choose Mathlib projectiveResolution X (whose existence is proved). Compose ProjectiveResolution.isoExt with homology of the projective edge and the inverse of homology of the injective edge. Prove naturality of isoExt by unopping isoLeftDerivedObj_inv_naturality and using homologyOp_hom_naturality, then cancelling the homologyUnop isomorphisms. For a morphism lift it using ProjectiveResolution.lift; lift_commutes_zero gives augmentation compatibility. Apply homology to the two proved edge squares. Cancel the invertible injective edge and substitute these squares and isoExt naturality. NatIso.ofComponents packages the resulting natural linear isomorphism. Every step is proved in Lean; no homotopy-coherence obligation is left.
